name: Mayrhofen
kurzbeschreibung: The heart of the Zillertal – famous for its legendary snowboarding event and breathtaking hiking trails in summer.
text:
Overview

Mayrhofen is the internationally celebrated tourism capital of the Zillertal valley in the Schwaz district of Tyrol. Situated at an altitude of 633 metres in the upper Zillertal, the market town lies precisely where the valley branches into four dramatic high-alpine tributary glens: the Tuxertal, Zemmgrund, Stilluptal, and Zillergrund. Home to approximately 4,000 residents, Mayrhofen serves as the bustling gateway to the High Alps Nature Park Zillertal Alps. Flanked by its iconic peaks, Mount Penken (2,095 m) and Mount Ahorn (2,973 m), the world-famous alpine destination unites mountaineering tradition, state-of-the-art cableway engineering, lively nightlife, and authentic Tyrolean folklore.

History

Human settlement in the valley basin dates back to the early Middle Ages, with the locality first documented around 1200 under the name Mairhof, signifying a principal manorial estate belonging to the Archbishopric of Salzburg. For centuries, the Ziller river demarcated the border between Tyrol and Salzburg right through the town. The late-Gothic parish church of Our Lady was updated in baroque elegance in the 18th century. In the late 19th century, pioneering alpinists exploring summits around the historic Berlin Mountain Hut ignited modern mountain tourism. The opening of the narrow-gauge Zillertal Railway in 1902 made Mayrhofen easily accessible from across the globe, establishing its enduring reputation as a premier world resort.

Getting There

Mayrhofen enjoys straightforward international travel connections. Motorists leave the A12 Inntal Autobahn at the Wiesing/Zillertal exit, following the well-maintained B169 Zillertal federal highway southward for roughly 30 kilometres straight to Mayrhofen. Rail passengers arrive at the major ÖBB junction in Jenbach in the Inn Valley, where the historic Zillertal Railway operates modern passenger trains every 30 minutes straight into Mayrhofen station. A dense network of electric ski buses and regional coaches connects all cable cars and side valleys.

Tips

In winter, the Mountopolis ski network on Mount Penken and Mount Ahorn delivers premier snow sports: thrill-seekers can conquer the legendary Harakiri, Austria's steepest groomed slope featuring a 78-percent gradient, while the Ahornbahn operates as Austria's largest aerial tramway cabin carrying 160 passengers. In summer, excursions to high-alpine reservoirs such as the Schlegeis Dam provide stunning walks along dam crests and thrilling via ferratas. Hikers can tackle stages of the famed Berlin High Trail through pristine glacial landscapes, before unwinding at the Mayrhofen Adventure Pool with its spa facilities.
